children.translated_text: For nourishment I take you, for good prosperity.
You are the winds.

children.text: devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatu śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> set you in motion for the very best rite.
Swell with fullness, inviolable cows, as the gods' portion for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: mā vaḥ stena īśata māghaśaṃso dhruvā asmin gopatau syāta bahvīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let no thief rule over you, nor any evil-speaker; be firm, numerous, under this lord of cattle.
Protect the sacrificer's cattle.
You are seated among the cows; the demon is burned away, the hostile foe is burned away.

children.text: preyam agād dhiṣaṇā barhir accha manunā kṛtā svadhayā vitaṣṭā
children.translated_text: The inspired prayer, made by <s>Manu</s> and fashioned by its own power, has gone forward gladly toward the sacred grass,
with it the sages bring the gods here in front.

children.text: devānāṃ pariṣūtam asi viṣṇoḥ stupo 'tisṛṣṭo gavāṃ bhāgo devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ barhir devasadanaṃ dāmi ||
children.translated_text: You are what has been spread around for the gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s tuft, released, the cows' share; at the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I cut you as sacred grass, the gods' seat.

children.text: atas tvaṃ barhiḥ śatavalśaṃ viroha sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhema ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, sacred grass, grow up with a hundred shoots; may we grow widely with a thousand shoots.

children.text: ayupitā yonir adityā rāsnāsīndrāṇyāḥ saṃnahanaṃ pūṣā te granthiṃ grathnātu sa te mā sthād indrasya tvā bāhubhyām udyacche bṛhaspater mūrdhnāharāmy urv antarikṣaṃ vīhy adityās tvā pṛṣṭhe sādayāmi ||
children.translated_text: You are the uninjured womb, the girdle of <s>Aditi</s>, the fastening of <s>Indrāṇī</s>; let <s>Pūṣan</s> tie your knot, and let it not come loose for you. With the arms of <s>Indra</s> I lift you up; with the head of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> I carry you. Go through the broad midspace; I set you on the back of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: pra vo vājā abhidyavo haviṣmanto ghṛtācyā
children.translated_text: For you the strong ones, shining toward us, rich in oblation and dripping with ghee,
go to the gods, desirous of favor.

children.text: upa tvā juhvo mama ghṛtācīr yantu haryata
children.translated_text: Let my ladles, dripping with ghee, come near you, lovely one;
<s>Agni</s>, accept our oblations.

children.text: ud agne tava tad ghṛtād arcī rocatā āhutam
children.translated_text: Up, <s>Agni</s>, from that ghee may your flame shine, kindled by the offering,
settling at the mouth of the ladle.

children.text: prajā agne saṃvāsayehāśāś ca paśubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, make offspring dwell together here, along with the regions and the cattle;

children.text: rāṣṭrāṇy asmin dhehi yāny āsant savituḥ save ||
children.translated_text: place in this man the dominions that were at <s>Savitṛ</s>'s impulse.

children.text: ayaṃ te yonir ṛtviyo yato jāto arocathāḥ
children.translated_text: This is your proper womb, from which, when born, you shone forth;

children.text: taṃ jānann agnā āroha tato no vardhayā rayim ||
children.translated_text: knowing it, <s>Agni</s>, ascend it, and from there increase wealth for us.

children.text: āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir akramīd asadan mātaraṃ puraḥ
children.translated_text: This speckled cow has stepped forward; she has sat before her mother,
and going toward her father, toward heaven.
With thirty abodes she shines forth; speech is invoked for the flying one;
the mighty one has made heaven manifest.

children.text: antaś caraty arṇave asya prāṇād apānataḥ
children.translated_text: He moves within the flood, from its in-breathing and out-breathing;
the sun faces you two with the days.

children.text: ito jajñe prathamaṃ svād yoner adhi jātavedāḥ
children.translated_text: From here <s>Jātavedas</s> was first born, from his own womb;

children.text: sa gāyatryā triṣṭubhā jagatyānuṣṭubhā ca devebhyo havyā vahatu prajānan ||
children.translated_text: let him, knowing, carry oblations to the gods with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Jagatī</s>, and the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: yo no agniḥ pitaro hṛtsv antar amartyo martyaṃ āviveśa
children.translated_text: That <s>Agni</s> of ours, immortal, who among the fathers entered the mortal within their hearts,

children.text: tam ātmani parigṛhṇīmasīha ned eṣo asmān avahāya parāyat ||
children.translated_text: we take hold of him here in ourselves, lest he go away, abandoning us.

children.text: dohyā ca te dugdhabhṛc corvarī te te bhāgadheyaṃ prayacchāmi tābhyāṃ tvādadhe gharmaḥ śiras tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhava purīṣam asi yat te śukra śukraṃ jyotis tena rucā rucam aśīthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your milch cow and your milk-bearing one, your fertile one: I assign your share to those two. From you the gharma is set down; the head is that Agni. Be dear together with the cattle. You are the fertile substance. With that bright, bright light of yours, with that radiance, may you attain radiance.

children.text: mayi gṛhṇāmy aham agre agniṃ saha prajayā varcasā dhanena
children.translated_text: I take <s>Agni</s> first into myself, together with offspring, brilliance, and wealth;

children.text: mayi kṣatraṃ mayi rāyo dadhāmi madema śatahimāḥ suvīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I place sovereignty in myself, I place riches in myself; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in good heroes.

children.text: bhūr bhuvo 'ṅgirasāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratenādadhe 'gneṣ ṭvā devasya vratenādadha indrasya tvā marutvato vratenādadhe manoṣ ṭvā grāmaṇyo vratenādadhe ||
children.translated_text: With bhūr and bhuvaḥ, by the vow of the <s>Aṅgiras</s> gods, I set you down; by the vow of the god <s>Agni</s> I set you down; by the vow of <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s> I set you down; by the vow of <s>Manu</s> the village-leader I set you down.

children.text: āchadi tvā chando dadhe dyaur mahnāsi bhūmir bhūnā
children.translated_text: I cover you; I place the meter over you. Heaven, by greatness, are you; earth, by being,

children.text: tasyās te devy adita upasthe 'nnādam agnim annapatyāyādadhe ||
children.translated_text: in her lap, O divine <s>Aditi</s>, I set down <s>Agni</s>, the eater of food, for lordship over food.

children.text: agnā āyūṃṣi pavase 'gnir ṛṣir agne pavasva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, you purify lifetimes; <s>Agni</s> is the seer. <s>Agni</s>, purify yourself.

children.text: yā vājinn agneḥ pavamānā priyā tanūs tām āvaha yā vājinn agneḥ pāvakā priyā tanūs tām āvaha yā vājinn agneḥ śuciḥ priyā tanūs tām āvaha ||
children.translated_text: O prize-winning one, bring here that dear body of <s>Agni</s> which is purifying; O prize-winning one, bring here that dear body of <s>Agni</s> which is bright; O prize-winning one, bring here that dear body of <s>Agni</s> which is pure.

children.text: yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna udyant samudrād uta vā purīṣāt
children.translated_text: When you neighed at first, being born, rising from the ocean or from the fertile substance,

children.text: śyenā te pakṣā hariṇota bāhū upastutyaṃ janima tat te arvan ||
children.translated_text: your wings were eagles, your arms antelopes: that birth of yours, O steed, is worthy of praise.

children.text: ojase balāya tvodyacche vṛṣṇe śuṣmāya sapatnatūr asi vṛtratūḥ ||
children.translated_text: For vigor, for strength, I lift you up; for virile force, for might. You are an overcomer of rivals, an overcomer of obstruction.

children.text: prācīm anu pradiśaṃ prehi vidvān agner agne puro agnir bhaveha
children.translated_text: Go forward along the eastern quarter, knowing; before <s>Agni</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, be <s>Agni</s> here.

children.text: viśvā āśā dīdyad vibhāhy ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade catuṣpade ||
children.translated_text: Shining to all directions, gleam widely; place nourishment for us, for two-footed and four-footed beings.

children.text: abhyasthāṃ viśvāḥ pṛtanā arātīs tad agnir āha tad u soma āha
children.translated_text: I have stood against all battles and hostilities; that <s>Agni</s> has said, that <s>Soma</s> has said,

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ savitendras tad āha pūṣā nā ādhāt sukṛtasya loke ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Indra</s> have said it; may <s>Pūṣan</s> place us in the world of the well-done deed.

children.text: bhuvaḥ svar aṅgirasāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratenādadhe 'gneṣ ṭvā devasya vratenādadha indrasya tvā marutvato vratenādadhe manoṣ ṭvā grāmaṇyo vratenādadhe ||
children.translated_text: With bhuvaḥ and svar, by the vow of the <s>Aṅgiras</s> gods, I set you down; by the vow of the god <s>Agni</s> I set you down; by the vow of <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s> I set you down; by the vow of <s>Manu</s> the village-leader I set you down.

children.text: āchadi tvā chando dadhe dyaur mahnāsi bhūmir bhūnā
children.translated_text: I cover you; I place the meter over you. Heaven, by greatness, are you; earth, by being,

children.text: tasyās te devy adita upasthe 'nnādam agnim annapatyāyādadhe ||
children.translated_text: in her lap, O divine <s>Aditi</s>, I set down <s>Agni</s>, the eater of food, for lordship over food.

children.text: yat te śukra śukraṃ jyotiḥ śukraṃ dhāmājasraṃ tena tvādadhe ||
children.translated_text: With that bright, bright light of yours, that bright and unfailing splendor, I set you down.

children.text: iḍāyās tvā pade vayaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā adhi
children.translated_text: At the place of <s>Iḍā</s>, upon the navel of the earth, we
place you, <s>Jātavedas</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, to carry the oblation.

children.text: samrāṭ ca svarāṭ cāgne ye te tanvau tābhyāṃ mā ūrjaṃ yaccha virāṭ ca prabhūś cāgne ye te tanvau tābhyāṃ mā ūrjaṃ yaccha vibhūś ca paribhūś cāgne ye te tanvau tābhyāṃ mā ūrjaṃ yaccha ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, with those two bodies of yours, sovereign and self-ruling, grant me nourishment; O <s>Agni</s>, with those two bodies of yours, widely-ruling and overpowering, grant me nourishment; O <s>Agni</s>, with those two bodies of yours, all-pervading and encompassing, grant me nourishment.

children.text: samudrād ūrmir madhumaṃ udārad upāṃśunā sam amṛtatvam ānaṭ
children.translated_text: From the ocean the honeyed wave has arisen; by the upāṃśu draught it has reached immortality.

children.text: ghṛtasya nāma guhyaṃ yad asti jihvā devānām amṛtasya nābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The secret name of ghee that exists is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.

children.text: vayaṃ nāma prabravāmā ghṛtasyāsmin yajñe dhārayāmā namobhiḥ
children.translated_text: We proclaim our name; in this sacrifice we sustain the stream of ghee with acts of homage.

children.text: upa brahmā śṛṇavañ śasyamānaṃ catuḥśṛṅgo 'vamīd gaura etat ||
children.translated_text: May the <s>brahman</s> priest hear what is being recited nearby; this four-horned bull has bellowed forth.

children.text: catvāri śṛṅgā trayo asya pādā dve śīrṣe sapta hastāso asya
children.translated_text: Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, seven are his hands.

children.text: tredhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti maho devo martyaṃ ātatāna ||
children.translated_text: Bound in three ways, the bull roars; the great god has stretched himself over the mortal.

children.text: ye agnayaḥ samanasā oṣadhīṣu vanaspatiṣu praviṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: The fires which, of one mind, have entered into the herbs and the forest trees,

children.text: te virājam abhisaṃyantu sarvā ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade catuṣpade ||
children.translated_text: let all those come together with Viraj. Place nourishment for us, for two-footed and four-footed beings.

children.text: sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvāḥ sapta ṛṣayaḥ sapta dhāma priyāṇi
children.translated_text: Seven are your kindling-sticks, O <s>Agni</s>; seven your tongues; seven the seers; seven your dear abodes.

children.text: sapta ṛtvijaḥ saptadhā tvā yajanti sapta hotrā ṛtuthā nu vidvānt sapta yonīr āpṛṇasva ghṛtena svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Seven officiants worship you in seven ways; knowing the seven oblations according to season, fill the seven wombs with ghee. Svaha.

children.text: ye agnayo divo ye pṛthivyāḥ samāgachantīṣam ūrjaṃ vasānāḥ
children.translated_text: The fires that are of heaven and those of earth, coming together clothed in refreshment and strength,

children.text: te asmā agnaye draviṇaṃ dattveṣṭāḥ prītā āhutibhājo bhūtvā yathālokaṃ punar astaṃ pareta svāhā ||
children.translated_text: let them give wealth to this <s>Agni</s>. Having been worshipped, pleased, and sharers in the oblation, let them go back home each to his proper world. Svaha.
<s>Varuna</s>, firm in his vow, has sat down among the dwellings,
the wise one, for sovereignty.

children.text: uta no 'hir budhnyaḥ śṛṇotv aja ekapāt pṛthivī samudraḥ
children.translated_text: And may <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> hear us, and <s>Aja Ekapad</s>, the earth, and the ocean.

children.text: stutā mantrāḥ kaviśastā avantu na enā rājan haviṣā mādayasva ||
children.translated_text: May the praised mantras, lauded by poets, help us. O king, take delight in this oblation.

children.text: pra nūnaṃ brahmaṇaspatir mantraṃ vadaty ukthyam
children.translated_text: Now <s>Brahmanaspati</s> speaks forth the mantra worthy of recitation,

children.text: yasminn indro varuṇo mitro aryamā devā okāṃsi cakrire ||
children.translated_text: in which <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuna</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and the gods made their dwelling-places.

children.text: gharmaḥ śiras tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhava purīṣam asi yachā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yor arko jyotis tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhava purīṣam asi yachā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yor vātaḥ prāṇas tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhava purīṣam asi yachā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The heat is the head; this <s>Agni</s> here is dear together with the cattle. You are the fertile substance; grant welfare and blessing to offspring and descendants. The chant is the light; this <s>Agni</s> here is dear together with the cattle. You are the fertile substance; grant welfare and blessing to offspring and descendants. The wind is the breath; this <s>Agni</s> here is dear together with the cattle. You are the fertile substance; grant welfare and blessing to offspring and descendants.
Cook food for us free from poison.
Let heaven and earth be made ready; let the waters and herbs be made ready.

children.text: kalpantām agnayaḥ pṛthaṅ mama jyaiṣṭhyāya savratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the fires, each separately and sharing the same vow, be made ready for my pre-eminence.

children.text: ye agnayaḥ samanasā oṣadhīṣu vanaspatiṣu praviṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: The fires which, of one mind, have entered into the herbs and the forest trees,

children.text: te virājam abhisaṃyantu sarvā ūrjaṃ no dhatta dvipade catuṣpade ||
children.translated_text: let all those come together with Viraj. Bestow nourishment upon us, upon two-footed and four-footed beings.

children.text: prajāpatir vā idam agra āsīt taṃ vīrudho 'bhyarohann asuryo vā etā yad oṣadhayas tā atitiṣighiṣann atiṣṭighaṃ nāśaknot so 'śocat so 'tapyata tato 'gnir asṛjyata tam agniṃ sṛṣṭaṃ vīrudhāṃ tejo 'gacchat tā aśuṣyan na tataḥ purāśuṣyan sa prajāpatir agnim ādhattemā evāsahā iti tā asahata tat sāḍhyai vāvaiṣa ādhīyate tad yathādo vasantāśiśire 'gnir vīrudhaḥ sahata evaṃ sapatnaṃ bhrātṛvyam avartiṃ sahate ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatte
children.translated_text: <s>Prajapati</s> alone was this in the beginning. The plants mounted upon him. These herbs are indeed asurya; they tried to overmaster him, but he could not overmaster them. He grieved and became heated; from that <s>Agni</s> was created. When that created <s>Agni</s> went to the brilliance of the plants, they dried up; before that they had not dried. <s>Prajapati</s> established <s>Agni</s>, thinking, 'I have overcome these.' He overcame them. This fire is established precisely for overcoming. Just as, in spring and winter, fire overcomes the plants, so he overcomes a rival, a kinsman-enemy, and misfortune, who, knowing thus, establishes <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: etāvad vā asyā anabhimṛtaṃ yāvad vediḥ parigṛhītā tām uddhatyāpa upasṛjyāgnim ādhatte yajñiyām evaināṃ medhyāṃ kṛtvādhatte 'gner vā iyaṃ sṛṣṭād abibhed ati mā dhakṣyatīti yad apa upasṛjyāgnim ādhatte 'syā anatidāhāyaiṣā vai prajāpateḥ sarvatā tanūr yad āpaḥ sarvata enaṃ prajāḥ sarvataḥ paśavo 'bhi puṇyena bhavanti ya evaṃ vidvān apa upasṛjyāgnim ādhatte
children.translated_text: So much of this earth is uninjured as is enclosed by the altar. Having dug it up, poured water upon it, he establishes <s>Agni</s>; having made this earth fit for sacrifice and pure, he establishes it. This earth feared <s>Agni</s> after he had been created, thinking, 'He will burn me excessively.' When, after pouring water, he establishes <s>Agni</s>, it is so that she may not be overburned. The waters are indeed <s>Prajapati</s>'s body in every direction. From every side his offspring and from every side his cattle become surrounded by merit, who, knowing thus, establishes <s>Agni</s> after pouring water.

children.text: yāvad vai varāhasya caṣālaṃ tāvatīyam agra āsīd yad varāhavihatam upāsyāgnim ādhatta imām eva tan nāpārāḍ asyā enaṃ mātrāyām adhyādhatte tasmād eṣā varāhāya vimradata eṣa hy asyā mātrāṃ bibharti devapāṇayo vai nāmāsurā āsaṃs te devagavīr apājaṃs tā anvagacchaṃs tā abhyājaṃs tāsāṃ payo 'hīyata te 'bruvan yad vā āsāṃ varam abhūt tad ahāsteti tad varāho bhūtvāsurebhyo 'dhi devān āgacchat tasmād varāhaṃ gāvo 'nudhāvanti svaṃ payo jānānās tad yāvatpriyam eva paśūnāṃ dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ payas tāvatpriyaḥ paśūnāṃ dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān varāhavihatam upāsyāgnim ādhatte
children.translated_text: As far as a boar's snout reaches, so far this earth was in the beginning. When he places down earth dug up by a boar and establishes <s>Agni</s>, he thereby does not fail to obtain this earth; he establishes him upon her measure. Therefore she is soft for the boar, for he bears her measure. There were Asuras named <s>Devapani</s>; they drove away the gods' cows. The gods followed them, attacked them, and the milk of those cows was left behind. They said, 'What was best in them, that has been left.' That, becoming a boar, came from the Asuras to the gods. Therefore cows run after a boar, knowing their own milk. As dear as milk is to animals, two-footed and four-footed, so dear does he become to animals, two-footed and four-footed, who, knowing thus, places down boar-dug earth and establishes <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: etad vā asyā anabhimṛtaṃ yad valmīko yad valmīkavapām upakīryāgnim ādhatte 'syā evainam anabhimṛte 'dhyādhatte raso vā eṣo 'syā udaiṣad yad valmīko yad valmīkavapām upakīryāgnim ādhatte 'syā evainaṃ rase 'dhyādhatta ūrg vā eṣo 'syā udaiṣad yad valmīko yad valmīkavapām upakīryāgnim ādhatte 'syā evainam ūrj adhyādhatte prajāpater vā eṣa stano yad valmīko yad valmīkavapām upakīryāgnim ādhatte prajāpatir evāsmai stanam apidadhāty annādyam asmā avarunddhe 'kṣudhyatāṃ svānāṃ puraḥsthātā bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: This much of her is uninjured, namely an anthill. When he scatters anthill earth and establishes <s>Agni</s>, he establishes him upon this earth's uninjured part. This is her essence that has risen up, namely an anthill. When he scatters anthill earth and establishes <s>Agni</s>, he establishes him upon her essence. This is her nourishment that has risen up, namely an anthill. When he scatters anthill earth and establishes <s>Agni</s>, he establishes him upon her nourishment. This is <s>Prajapati</s>'s breast, namely an anthill. When he scatters anthill earth and establishes <s>Agni</s>, <s>Prajapati</s> places his breast before him; he secures food for him. He becomes one who stands at the head of his own people, not subject to hunger, who knows thus.

children.text: etāvad vā amuṣyā iha yajñiyaṃ yad ūṣā yad ūṣān upakīryāgnim ādhatte 'muṣyā evainaṃ yajñiye 'dhyādhatte na vā anūṣarihaḥ paśavo reto dadhate yad ūṣān upakīryāgnim ādhatte reta evaitad dadhāti paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai prajātyai
children.translated_text: Just so much of that world here is fit for sacrifice as is the <s>ūṣā</s>. When, after scattering <s>ūṣā</s>, he lays down the fire, he lays it down upon what is fit for sacrifice in that very world. For cattle do not place seed in what is without <s>ūṣā</s> here. When, after scattering <s>ūṣā</s>, he lays down the fire, he thereby places seed, for the prosperity and procreation of the cattle.

children.text: eṣa vā agnir vaiśvānaro yad asā ādityaḥ sa yad ihāsīt tasyaitad bhasma yat sikatā yat sikatā upakīryāgnim ādhatte sva evainaṃ yonau sve bhasmann ādhatte
children.translated_text: This fire, indeed, is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, namely yonder <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). What was here of him, that is his ash, namely the sand. When, after scattering sand, he lays down the fire, he lays it down in its own womb, in its own ash.

children.text: śithirā vā iyam agra āsīt tāṃ prajāpatiḥ śarkarābhir adṛṃhad yaccharkarā upakīryāgnim ādhatta imām eva tad dṛṃhati dhṛtyai tad yathemāṃ prajāpatiḥ śarkarābhir adṛṃhad evam asmin paśavo dṛṃhante ya evaṃ vidvāñ śarkarā upakīryāgnim ādhatta indro vai vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tasya yā vipruṣā āsaṃs tāḥ śarkarā abhavan yaccharkarā upakīryāgnim ādhatte vajram eva sapatnāya bhrātṛvyāya praharati yaṃ dviṣyāt tam tarhi manasā dhyāyed vajram evāsmai praharati stṛṇuta eva
children.translated_text: This earth was loose at first. <s>Prajāpati</s> made it firm with gravel. When, after scattering gravel, he lays down the fire, he thereby makes this earth firm, for stability. And just as <s>Prajāpati</s> made this earth firm with gravel, so cattle become firm in him who, knowing thus, lays down the fire after scattering gravel. <s>Indra</s>, indeed, hurled the thunderbolt at <s>Vṛtra</s>; the splinters of it that there were became gravel. When, after scattering gravel, he lays down the fire, he hurls the thunderbolt at his rival, his kinsman-enemy. Whomever he should hate, he should then think of him in his mind; he hurls the thunderbolt at him and cuts him down.

children.text: purīṣīti vai gṛhamedhinam āhuḥ purīṣasya khalu vā etan nirūpaṃ yad ākhukirir yad ākhukirim upakīryāgnim ādhatte purīṣī gṛhamedhī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: They call a householder '<s>purīṣin</s>' (rich in manure). For this, namely what is dug up by mice, is indeed a form of manure. When, after scattering what is dug up by mice, he lays down the fire, the householder becomes rich in manure.

children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, were unable to divide <s>Agni</s>. When they carried him eastward, he was wholly in front; when they carried him westward, he was wholly behind. They carried him forward with a horse as the one drawing in front; that is why the horse has the state of being the front-drawer, the leader in front. Because of the division of <s>Agni</s>, a horse is given at the establishment of the sacred fire. For the fire of the man who does not give a horse at the agnyādheya is unseparated and unestablished; but the man who gives a horse at the agnyādheya, for the sake of division, establishes it only after dividing it. With a stoma in front the gods defeated the <s>Asuras</s>; and this, namely the horse, is indeed the stoma. When they lead the horse in front, it is for victory; having conquered, he establishes the fire. The eye of <s>Prajāpati</s> swelled up; the swelling that belonged to it became the horse. When they lead the horse in front, they place sight in the sacrificer himself. It should not be let go facing away. If he were to let it go facing away, sight would abandon the sacrificer and he would become blind. It is to be established after being held back toward him; he has held sight back for the sacrificer himself. It should not be established on its track, for he would make it resident there, and <s>Rudra</s> would become one who threatens his cattle. It is to be established from the side, either from here or from there; he does not make it resident, and <s>Paśupati</s> becomes harmless toward his cattle. The gods sent the <s>Gāyatrī</s> toward the sacrifice; she came back empty. <s>Agni</s> gave her radiance, and that became the goat. When he gives a goat at the agnyādheya, he secures radiance itself. It is to be given to the <s>Agnīdh</s>; the <s>Agnīdh</s> is the mouth of the sacrifice, and by means of the mouth of the sacrifice he prospers the mouth of the sacrifice. He gives a milch cow and a draught ox; thereby he secures all vital power. For this is all vital power, namely the milch cow and the draught ox. These two are the mother and father of the sacrifice, namely the milch cow and the draught ox; ghee and milk come from the cow, and the sacrificial cake and the cooked oblation from the ox. Therefore they say, 'He who gives a milch cow and a draught ox at the agnyādheya secures a wish-milking cow.' Of those animals whose most abundant thriving he desires, he should give a female of that kind, one that has borne twice, and a castrated male that draws twice; that is a pair, for the thriving of cattle and for procreation. Speech is the soma-purchasing cow, a female that has borne twice; the soma-purchasing cow is vital power. When he gives a twice-bearing female of that vital power, he secures speech itself; he speaks beautifully, he who knows thus. A cushion made of all threads is to be given. This is the form of the meters, namely a cushion made of all threads. When he gives a cushion made of all threads, he secures the meters themselves. The meters are cattle; he secures cattle themselves. One born from the womb is unfit for sacrifice and impure, for he drinks human milk. He gives gold; by that he purifies himself. It is of a hundred mānas; man indeed has a lifespan of a hundred years and strength for a hundred. He obtains lifespan and strength. For the first two oblations two pieces of thirty mānas are to be given; for the later one, one of forty mānas. That has raised him upward; by that he becomes higher, more prosperous, and better. A man is, as it were, unborn so long as he has not established the fire. He is born only then, when he establishes the fire. The two should establish the fire wearing linen garments; these are to be given to the adhvaryu. Linen is the form of the caul; they thereby strip off the caul itself. After placing gold, suvarṇa, upon it, the fire is to be established. Gold is the radiance of <s>Agni</s>; he establishes him endowed with radiance. That should not be cast away. If he were to cast it away as it had been set down, then, if he cast it away, he would become brooding and hungry. Therefore it should not be cast away; he becomes free from brooding and free from hunger.

children.text: yo vā asyāyaṃ manuṣyo 'gnir etam upāsīno 'nnam atty etam upāsīnaḥ prajāṃ vindata etam upāsīnaṃ paśavā upatiṣṭhante yad etam abhāgadheyam utsādayeta tasmā āvṛścetānudhyāyī kṣodhukaḥ syāt tad ye vanaspataya āraṇyā ādyaṃ phalaṃ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ pacyante tasya parṇābhyāṃ yavamayaś cāpūpo vrīhimayaś ca saṃgṛhyopāsyādheyas tad enaṃ dvayaṃ bhāgadheyam abhyutsādayām akar grāmyaṃ cāraṇyaṃ ca tena tasmai nāvṛścate 'nanudhyāyy akṣodhuko bhavati yavo vai pūrva ṛtumukhe pacyata itaḥ khalu vā etaṃ prāñcam uddharanti tasmād yavamayaḥ paścopāsyo vrīhimayaḥ puras tad yasyertsed yavamayam eva tasya paścopāsyed vrīhimayaṃ puraḥ prajāpater vā etau stanau yajñam asya devā upajīvanti varṣaṃ manuṣyā annādyam asmā avarunddhe 'kṣudhyatāṃ svānāṃ puraḥsthātā bhavati ya evaṃ vedaitaddha sma vā āha keśī sātyakāmiḥ keśinaṃ dārbhyam annādaṃ janatāyā evam iva vayam etasmā agnyādheye 'nnam avārudhma yathaiṣo 'nnam atti tad āhuḥ sarvaṃ vāvaitasyedam annaṃ yajamānaṃ tv evāsyaitad āsann apidadhāti tad evaṃ veditor na tv evaṃ kartavā iti trir vā idaṃ prajāpatiḥ satyaṃ vyāharat ||
children.translated_text: Now, this human fire of his: while attending upon it he eats food; while attending upon it he obtains offspring; while he attends upon it, cattle attend upon him. If he were to cause this one, without its allotted share, to be driven away, then it would cut him off: he would become brooding and hungry. Therefore, among the forest trees whose first edible fruit ripens most abundantly, from two leaves of that tree he should collect and place near it a barley cake and a rice cake. Thus he has caused this twofold allotted share, domestic and forest, to be raised up for it. By that it does not cut him off; he becomes free from brooding and free from hunger. Barley indeed ripens first at the opening of the season. From here, indeed, they carry this fire eastward; therefore the barley cake is to be placed behind and the rice cake in front. If he should have a wish concerning someone, he should place only that person's barley cake behind and rice cake in front. These two are the breasts of <s>Prajāpati</s>; the gods live upon his sacrifice, and human beings upon the rain. He secures food to eat for him. He becomes one who stands before his own people without hunger, who knows thus. And indeed <s>Keśin Sātyakāmi</s> said to <s>Keśin Dārbhya</s>, an eater of food among the people: 'In this fire-establishment we have secured food for ourselves just as this man eats food.' They say: 'All this is indeed food for this sacrificer; but by this he merely covers its mouth.' One should know it thus, but one should not do it thus. Three times, indeed, <s>Prajāpati</s> uttered truth.

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ itīdaṃ vāva bhūr idaṃ bhuvo 'daḥ svas tad yo brāhmaṇa āṅgirasaḥ syāt tasyādadhyād bhūr bhuvo 'ṅgirasāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratenādadhā iti paścā bhuvaḥ svar iti puro dviḥ paścā dviḥ puras tad dvedhā yajñaḥ satye pratyaṣṭhād dvedhā yajñapatir atha yo brāhmaṇo vaiśvānaraḥ syāt tasyādadhyād bhūr bhuvo 'gneṣ ṭvā devasya vratenādadhā iti paścā bhuvaḥ svar iti puro dviḥ paścā dviḥ puras tad dvedhā yajñaḥ satye pratyaṣṭhād dvedhā yajñapatir atha rājanyasyādadhyād bhūr bhuva indrasya tvā marutvato vratenādadhā iti paścā bhuvaḥ svar iti puro dviḥ paścā dviḥ puras tad dvedhā yajñaḥ satye pratyaṣṭhād dvedhā yajñapatir aindro vai rājanyo devatayā mārutī viḍ viśā khalu vai rājanyo bhadro bhavati viśam asmā avarunddhe 'tha vaiśyasyādadhyād bhūr bhuvo manoṣ ṭvā grāmaṇyo vratenādadhā iti paścā bhuvaḥ svar iti puro dviḥ paścā dviḥ puras tad dvedhā yajñaḥ satye pratyaṣṭhād dvedhā yajñapatir grāmaṇīthyena khalu vai vaiśyo bhadro bhavati grāmaṇīthyam asmā avarunddhe 'gnir vai sṛṣṭa ulbam apalumpaṃ nāśaknot tasya prajāpatir āgneyapāvamānībhir ulbam apālumpad yad āgneyapāvamānībhir āśvatthīḥ samidha ādadhāty ulbam evāsyāpalumpati punāty enaṃ yathā śiśuṃ mātā reḍhi vatsaṃ vā gaur evam enaṃ reḍhy agner vai sṛṣṭasya tejā udadīpyata tad aśvatthaṃ prāviśad yad āśvatthīḥ samidha ādadhāti teja evāvarunddhe 'gnir vai sṛṣṭo bibibābhavann atiṣṭhad asamidhyamānaḥ sa prajāpatir abibhen māṃ vāvāyaṃ hiṃsiṣyatīti taṃ śamyā samaindhat tam aśamayat tacchamyāḥ śamītvaṃ yacchamīmayīḥ samidha ādadhāti sam enam inddhe śamayaty eva sa śaṃ yajamānāya bhavati śaṃ paśubhyo devā yatrorjaṃ vyabhajanta tata udumbarā udatiṣṭhad yad audumbarīṃ samidham ādadhāty ūrjam evāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>.' This here is truly <s>bhūr</s>, this is <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, that is <s>svaḥ</s>. If he is a Brahmin of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> lineage, one should establish it for him, saying, '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>; with the vow of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> gods I establish you,' behind; '<s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>,' in front; twice behind and twice in front. Thus the sacrifice is established twofold in truth, and the lord of the sacrifice twofold. Then, if he is a Brahmin connected with <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, one should establish it for him, saying, '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>; with the vow of the god <s>Agni</s> I establish you,' behind; '<s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>,' in front; twice behind and twice in front. Thus the sacrifice is established twofold in truth, and the lord of the sacrifice twofold. Then for a <s>rājanya</s> one should establish it, saying, '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>; with the vow of <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s> I establish you,' behind; '<s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>,' in front; twice behind and twice in front. Thus the sacrifice is established twofold in truth, and the lord of the sacrifice twofold. The <s>rājanya</s> is indeed <s>Aindra</s> by deity, and the people are <s>Māruta</s>; for, through the people, the <s>rājanya</s> becomes prosperous. He secures the people for him. Then for a <s>vaiśya</s> one should establish it, saying, '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>; with the vow of <s>Manu</s> the village-leader I establish you,' behind; '<s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>,' in front; twice behind and twice in front. Thus the sacrifice is established twofold in truth, and the lord of the sacrifice twofold. The <s>vaiśya</s> indeed becomes prosperous through village-leadership; he secures village-leadership for him. When <s>Agni</s> had been created, he could not strip off the caul. <s>Prajāpati</s> stripped off his caul with the <s>Āgneya-Pāvamānī</s> verses. When he lays down aśvattha fuel-sticks with the <s>Āgneya-Pāvamānī</s> verses, he strips off his caul and purifies him. As a mother licks a child, or a cow her calf, so he licks him clean. The splendor of <s>Agni</s>, when he had been created, blazed forth; it entered the aśvattha tree. When he lays down aśvattha fuel-sticks, he secures that very splendor. When <s>Agni</s> had been created, he stood there, terrifying, not kindled. <s>Prajāpati</s> was afraid: 'This one will surely injure me.' He kindled him with a śamī stick and pacified him; that is why the śamī has its quality of pacification. When he lays down śamī fuel-sticks, he kindles him completely and pacifies him. He becomes auspicious for the sacrificer and auspicious for the cattle. Where the gods divided nourishment, from there the udumbara tree arose. When he lays down an udumbara fuel-stick, he secures nourishment itself.

children.text: vipriyo vā eṣa paśubhir ādhīyata eṣa hi rudro yad agnis tad vācayed gharmaḥ śiras tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhava purīṣam asīti tad enaṃ saṃpriyaṃ paśubhiḥ purīṣiṇam akar yat te śukra śukraṃ jyotis tena rucā rucam aśīthā iti rucam evainam ajīgamad eṣa vā agnir vaiśvānaro yad asā ādityo yad uttarato hared eṣo 'taḥ syād ayam ito jīvantam evainaṃ pradahet sa dakṣiṇata eva hāryaḥ sa yadā samayādhvaṃ gacched atha yajamāno varaṃ dadyāt tad virājaṃ madhyato 'dhita virāḍ evāsyāgnīn vidadhate paśavo vai virāṭ paśūn vā etan madhyato 'dhitāsṛṣṭo vā agnir āsīd atha prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā andhe tamasīmāṃllokān anuvyanaśyan so 'śocat so 'tapyata tato 'gnir asṛjyata tam agniṃ sṛṣṭam adho vyadadhāt taṃ yā asmiṃl loka āsaṃs tā abhisamāvartanta taṃ kulphadaghnam udagṛhṇāt taṃ yā uttarasmiṃlloka āsaṃs tā abhisamāvartanta taṃ jānudaghnaṃ taṃ nābhidaghnaṃ tam aṃsadaghnaṃ taṃ karṇadaghnam udagṛhṇāt taṃ yā uttarasmiṃl loka āsaṃs tā abhisamāvartanta taṃ karṇadaghnaṃ nātyudgṛhyo yat karṇadaghnam atyudgṛhṇīyād yajamāno varṣiṣṭhaḥ paśūnāṃ yajamānam upariṣṭād agnir abhyavadahet tad āhuḥ katham adyaitam brahmaṇāhitaṃ pracyāvayeyuḥ śithiraṃ vāvainam etad akaḥ parainaṃ vapatīti tam anidhāyaivātha jānudaghnam udgṛhṇīyād atha nābhidaghnam athāṃsadaghnaṃ tad yathaiva prajāpatiṃ prajā ebhyo lokebhyo 'bhisamāvartantaivam eva yajamānaṃ paśava ebhyo lokebhyo 'bhisamāvartante ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatte 'gninā vai devatayā viṣṇunā yajñena devā asurān pravlīya vajreṇānvavāsṛjan yaḥ sapatnavān bhrātṛvyavān vā syāt tasya rathacakraṃ trir anuparivartayeyus tad yathaiva devā asurān agninā devatayā viṣṇunā yajñena pravlīya vajreṇānvavāsṛjann evam eva yajamānaḥ sapatnaṃ bhrātṛvyam agninā devatayā viṣṇunā yajñena pravlīya vajreṇānvavasṛjati ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatte ||
children.translated_text: This one, indeed, when established, becomes disagreeable to the cattle, for <s>Agni</s> is <s>Rudra</s>. Therefore he should make him recite: 'The gharma is the head; this <s>Agni</s> here is dear together with the cattle. You are the fertile substance.' Thus he made him dear together with the cattle and rich in fertile substance. 'With that bright, bright light of yours, by that radiance you have attained radiance': he thereby brought him to radiance. This fire is indeed <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, namely yonder <s>Āditya</s> (sun). If he were to carry it from the north, that one would be from there and this one from here; he would burn this living man. Therefore it is to be carried from the south. When he goes midway along the road, then the sacrificer should give a boon. That is the <s>Virāj</s> set in the middle; they thereby dispose his fires by means of <s>Virāj</s>. Cattle are <s>Virāj</s>; cattle indeed are thereby set in the middle. <s>Agni</s> had been created loose. Then <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. They, in blind darkness, spread through these worlds. He grieved and became heated; from that <s>Agni</s> was created. Having created that <s>Agni</s>, he placed him below. Those creatures that were in this world turned toward him. He lifted him up ankle-deep. Those that were in the next world turned toward him. He lifted him knee-deep, then navel-deep, then shoulder-deep, then ear-deep. Those that were in the still higher world turned toward him. One should not raise him beyond ear-depth. If he were to raise him beyond ear-depth, since the sacrificer is the highest among the cattle, <s>Agni</s> would burn the sacrificer from above. They say, 'How could they dislodge this one, established by sacred formulation?' In fact one has made him loose by this: 'Cast him away beyond.' Without setting him down, then, one should lift him knee-deep, then navel-deep, then shoulder-deep. Just as creatures turned toward <s>Prajāpati</s> from these worlds, so cattle turn toward the sacrificer from these worlds, when, knowing thus, he establishes <s>Agni</s>. With <s>Agni</s> as deity and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as sacrifice, the gods, having crushed the <s>Asuras</s>, pursued them with the thunderbolt. If a man has rivals or kinsman-enemies, they should roll a chariot-wheel around him three times. Just as the gods, with <s>Agni</s> as deity and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as sacrifice, crushed the <s>Asuras</s> and pursued them with the thunderbolt, so the sacrificer, with <s>Agni</s> as deity and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as sacrifice, crushes and pursues his rival, his kinsman-enemy, when, knowing thus, he establishes <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: eṣa vai prajāpatī rūpeṇa yat pūrṇā srug yat pūrṇāṃ srucaṃ juhoti prajāpatim evāpnoti sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā ity etāvatīr vā agnes tanvaḥ ṣoḍhā sapta sapta yo vā asyaitā agnim ādadhāno vitarṣayati vi ha tṛṣyati tā evāsya tarpayati śamīmayīs tisraḥ samidhā ādadhāti ghṛtānvaktā ghṛtastomyābhiḥ sam enam inddhe śamayaty eva sa śaṃ yajamānāya bhavati śaṃ paśubhyo ye vā eṣu triṣu lokeṣv agnayas te samāgacchanty asya draviṇam ādadāmahe 'ti no 'kramīddhavyavāḍ bhavatīti taj juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: This is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s> in form, namely a full offering-ladle. When he offers with a full ladle, he attains <s>Prajāpati</s> himself. 'Seven are your kindling-sticks, O <s>Agni</s>; seven your tongues': so many indeed are the bodies of <s>Agni</s>, sixfold, seven and seven. The man who, while establishing <s>Agni</s>, leaves these unsatisfied becomes utterly thirsty; he satisfies those very bodies of his. He lays down three śamī kindling-sticks, anointed with ghee, with verses praising ghee. He kindles him completely with them, and he pacifies him. He becomes auspicious for the sacrificer and auspicious for the cattle. The fires that are in these three worlds come together. 'We take wealth for him; he has not gone past us; let him become the oblation-bearer': with that he should offer.

children.text: ye agnayo divo ye pṛthivyāḥ samāgacchantīṣam ūrjaṃ vasānāḥ
children.translated_text: The fires that are of heaven, and those that are of earth, come together, clothed in refreshment and strength.

children.text: te asmā agnaye draviṇaṃ dattveṣṭāḥ prītā āhutibhājo bhūtvā yathālokaṃ punar astaṃ pareta ||
children.translated_text: Having given wealth to this <s>Agni</s>, having been worshipped, pleased, and sharers in the oblation, let them go back home, each to his proper world.

children.text: iḍāyās tvā pade vayaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā adhi
children.translated_text: At the place of <s>Iḍā</s>, upon the navel of the earth, we
place you, <s>Jātavedas</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, to carry the oblations.

children.text: iti havyavāham evainam akar agner vai sṛṣṭasya paśavo 'kṣyā avakśāya prāpatan sa prajāpatir vāravantīyam asṛjata tān avārayataitarhi khalu vā eṣa sṛjyate yarhy ādhīyate tad yathaitasmāt sṛṣṭāt paśavaḥ prāpatann evam asmād āhitātpaśavaḥ prapatanty eṣa hi rudro yad agnis tad ya evaṃ vidvān vāravantīyaṃ gāyate paśūn eva vārayate vāravantīyaṃ vai sṛṣṭvā prajāpatir yaṃ kāmam akāmayata tam ārdhnot tam eva kāmam ṛdhnoti yajamāno yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayamāno 'gnim ādhatte ya evaṃ vidvān vāravantīyaṃ gāyate 'gnir vai kravyād viśvadāvya imāṃl lokān adahat taṃ prajāpatir vāravantīyaṃ gāyamāno varaṇaṃ bibhrat pratyait tam aśamayad yad evāsya kravyād yad viśvadāvyaṃ tacchamayati ya evaṃ vidvān vāravantīyaṃ gāyate tasmād varaṇo yajñāvacaraḥ syān na tv enena juhuyād yad vā idaṃ sad yad bhūtaṃ yad bhavad yad bhaviṣyad yad ime antarā dyāvāpṛthivī tad vāmadevyaṃ tad evāvarunddhe ya evaṃ vidvān vāmadevyaṃ gāyate brahmaṇo vā eṣa raso yad yajñāyajñiyaṃ yad yajñāyajñiyaṃ gāyate brahmaṇy eva rasaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus he made him precisely the oblation-bearer. When <s>Agni</s> had been created, the cattle fell away from him, because of his consuming and devouring. <s>Prajāpati</s> created the <s>Vāravantīya</s> chant; by it he held them back. Indeed this one is created now when he is established. Just as the cattle fell away from that created one, so cattle fall away from this established one, for <s>Agni</s> is <s>Rudra</s>. Therefore the man who, knowing thus, sings the <s>Vāravantīya</s> holds back the cattle. Having created the <s>Vāravantīya</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> gained whatever desire he desired. The sacrificer gains that very desire which he desires when he establishes <s>Agni</s>, if, knowing thus, he sings the <s>Vāravantīya</s>. <s>Agni</s>, as a flesh-eater and all-consuming one, burned these worlds. <s>Prajāpati</s>, singing the <s>Vāravantīya</s> and carrying a varaṇa branch, went against him and pacified him. Whatever in him is flesh-eating, whatever is all-consuming, he pacifies that, when, knowing thus, he sings the <s>Vāravantīya</s>. Therefore the varaṇa should be used in the sacrificial performance, but one should not offer with it. Whatever this is that exists, whatever has been, whatever is becoming, whatever will be, whatever is here between heaven and earth: that is the <s>Vāmadevya</s>. He secures that very thing, when, knowing thus, he sings the <s>Vāmadevya</s>. The <s>Yajñāyajñiya</s> is the essence of <s>brahman</s>. When he sings the <s>Yajñāyajñiya</s>, he places essence in <s>brahman</s> itself.

children.text: agniṃ vai sṛṣṭaṃ prajāpatiḥ pavamānenāgrā upādhamat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, indeed, blew upon <s>Agni</s>, after he had been created, with the pavamāna verses at the front.

children.text: yat pavamānāya nirvapaty upaivainaṃ tad dhamati ||
children.translated_text: When he makes an offering for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>, thereby he blows upon him.
When it is for <s>Agni Pāvaka</s>, he purifies him.

children.text: yacchucaye yad evāsyāpūtaṃ tad etena punāti ||
children.translated_text: When it is for <s>Agni Śuci</s>, whatever of him is unpurified, that he purifies by this.

children.text: yat pavamānāya nirvapati paśavo vai pavamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he makes an offering for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>: cattle are indeed <s>Pavamāna</s>.
He thereby secures cattle.
When it is for <s>Agni Pāvaka</s>: food is indeed <s>Pāvaka</s>.
He thereby secures food.
When it is for <s>Agni Śuci</s>, he places radiance in him when he has been purified.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayetāpataraṃ pāpīyānt syād iti tasyaikamekaṃ havīṃṣi nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: For the man about whom he should wish, 'May he become lower and worse,' he should make the oblations one by one.
That has pulled him downward.
By that he becomes lower and worse.

children.text: atha yaṃ kāmayeta na vasīyānt syān na pāpīyān iti tasya sarvāṇi sākaṃ havīṃṣi nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: But for the man about whom he should wish, 'May he become neither better nor worse,' he should make all the oblations together.
That confines him.

children.text: tena sa na vasīyān na pāpīyān bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By that he becomes neither better nor worse.

children.text: atha yaṃ kāmayed uttaraṃ vasīyāñ śreyānt syād iti tasyāgnaye pavamānāya nirupyātha pāvakāya ca śucaye cottare haviṣī samānabarhiṣi nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: But for the man about whom he should wish, 'May he become higher, better, and superior,' after making an offering to <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>, he should make the two later oblations, to <s>Agni Pāvaka</s> and to <s>Agni Śuci</s>, on the same barhis.
That has raised him upward.

children.text: tena sa uttaraṃ vasīyāñ śreyān bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By that he becomes higher, better, and superior.

children.text: atha yasya triṣṭubhau vānuṣṭubhau vā jagatī vā saṃyājye syātām ati gāyatraṃ krāmet ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the two saṃyājya verses should be in triṣṭubh, anuṣṭubh, or jagatī meter, he would pass beyond the gāyatrī.
He would fall away short of the meters.

children.text: tad yasyertsed gāyatryā eva tasya saṃyājye kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the man whom he should wish to prosper, he should make his two saṃyājya verses in gāyatrī alone.

children.text: gāyatro hy agnir gāyatrachandāḥ sva evainaṃ yonau sve chandasi pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Agni</s> is gāyatrī, having the gāyatrī as his meter; he thereby establishes him in his own womb, in his own meter.
He should make an eleven-cup cake for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: agnir vai sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is indeed all the deities; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sacrifice.
He has thereby obtained both the deities and the sacrifice.

children.text: viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya tryuddhau ghṛte caruṃ nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: He should make a caru in ghee, in a threefold milk-mixture, for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.

children.text: yad viṣṇave viṣṇur vai yajño yajñam evālabdha ||
children.translated_text: In that it is for <s>Viṣṇu</s>: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is indeed the sacrifice; he thereby obtains the sacrifice.

children.text: yacchipiviṣṭaṃ paśavo vai śipiviṣṭaṃ paśūn evāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: In that it is for <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>: cattle are indeed <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>; he thereby secures cattle.

children.text: yat tryuddhau trayo vā ime lokā imān eva lokān āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: In that it is in a threefold milk-mixture: these worlds are three; he thereby obtains these worlds.

children.text: yad ghṛte tejo vai ghṛtaṃ teja evāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: In that it is in ghee: ghee is indeed brilliance; he thereby secures brilliance.
One desiring cattle should make a caru in ghee for <s>Āditya</s>.
Ghee is the milk of a milch cow; the rice-grains are those of a draught ox.
That is a pair, for the prosperity and procreation of cattle.
As a second offering he should next make an <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> sacrificial cake.
Thus more oblation has come near.
No one else has power over it.

children.text: yarhi vā etaṃ purā brāhmaṇā niravapaṃs tarhy eṣāṃ na kaścanaiśa ||
children.translated_text: For when the Brahmins formerly made this offering, then no one at all had power over them.

children.text: na hi vā etam idānīṃ nirvapanti ||
children.translated_text: For now they do not make this offering.
Therefore everyone has power over them.

children.text: yad āgneyas tejo vā agnis teja evāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: In that it is for <s>Agni</s>: <s>Agni</s> is indeed brilliance; he thereby secures brilliance.

children.text: yat saumyaḥ somo vai śukro brahmavarcasaṃ brahmavarcasam evāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: In that it is for <s>Soma</s>: <s>Soma</s> is indeed bright, brahmanic splendor; he thereby secures brahmanic splendor.

children.text: tad yo 'sā ādityo ghṛte carus taṃ brahmaṇe parihareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: That caru in ghee for yonder <s>Āditya</s> should be handed over to the <s>Brahman</s> priest.
Four should eat it.
An equal boon should be given to them.

children.text: catur vā idam agre mithunam audyataikaś caikā ca dvau ca dve ca trayaś ca tisraś ca catvāraś ca catasraś ca ||
children.translated_text: For in the beginning this fourfold pair was raised up: one male and one female, two males and two females, three males and three females, four males and four females.
That is a pair, for the prosperity and procreation of cattle.

children.text: phalgunīpūrṇamāse brāhmaṇasyādadhyāt phalgunīpūrṇamāso vā ṛtūnāṃ mukham agnir devatānāṃ brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇāṃ grīṣme rājanyasyādadhyād grīṣme vā indro vṛtram ahan vṛtraṃ khalu vai rājanyo bubhūṣan jighāṃsati śaradi vaiśyasyādadhyād annaṃ vai śarad annena vaiśyo bhadro bhavaty annādyam asmā avarunddhe yady anyasminn ṛtā ādadhīta yadi vā asmai sa eka ṛtuḥ śivaḥ syād athāsmā itare 'śivā duryoṇā bhaveyus tad yasyertset phalgunīpūrṇamāsa eva tasyādadhyāt tad asmai sarva ṛtavaḥ śivā bhavanti sarva enam ṛtavo jinvanti saṃvatsarasya vā etad āsyaṃ yat phalgunīpūrṇamāsyam ahar yat phalgunīpūrṇamāsyam ahar ādadhyāt saṃvatsarasyainam āsann apidadhyād dvyahe vā puraikāhe vādheyas tad dvitīyasya ṛtor abhigṛhṇāti nainaṃ saṃvatsarasyāsann apidadhāti tad yad dvitīyasya ṛtor abhigṛhṇāti dvitīyam eva sapatnasya bhrātṛvyasyendriyaṃ paśūn kṣetraṃ vṛñjāna eti kṛttikāsu brāhmaṇasyādadhyād āgneyīḥ kṛttikā āgneyo brāhmaṇaḥ sva evainaṃ yonau sve 'hann ādhatte prajāpater vā etañ śiro yat kṛttikā agnir āsyaṃ śīrṣṇānnam adyate 'nnādyam asmā avarunddhe sapta kṛttikāḥ sapta śīrṣan prāṇāḥ prāṇān asmin dadhāti rohiṇyāṃ paśukāmasyādadhyāt somasya vā etan nakṣatraṃ yad rohiṇī somo retodhā reto 'smin dadhāty ṛkṣā vā iyam agra āsīt tasyāṃ devā rohiṇyāṃ vīrudho 'rohayaṃs tad yathemā asyāṃ vīrudho rūḍhā evam asmin paśavo rohanti ya evaṃ vidvān rohiṇyām agnim ādhatte rohiṇyāṃ svargakāmasyādadhyād rohiṇyāṃ vai devāḥ svar āyan svar evaiti kālakāñjā vā asurā iṣṭakā acinvata divam ārokṣyāmā iti tān indro brāhmaṇo bruvāṇa upait sa etām iṣṭakām apy upādhatta prathamā iva divam ākramantātha sa tām āvṛhat te 'surāḥ pāpīyāṃso bhavanto 'pābhraṃśanta yā uttamā āstāṃ tau yamaśvā abhavatāṃ ye 'dhare ta ūrṇāvābhayo yāṃ tām iṣṭakām āvṛhat sā citrābhavad yaḥ sapatnavān bhrātṛvyavān vā syāt sa citrāyām agnim ādadhīta tad yathaitasyām āvṛḍhāyām asurāḥ pāpīyāṃso bhavanto 'pābhraṃśantaivam asya sapatno bhrātṛvyaḥ pāpīyān bhavann apabhraṃśate ya evaṃ vidvāṃś citrāyām agnim ādhatte yaḥ kāmayeta bhagy annādaḥ syām iti sa pūrvāsu phalgunīṣv agnim ādadhīta bhagasya vā etad ahar yat pūrvāḥ phalgunīr bhagy annādo bhavaty atha yaḥ kāmayeta dānakāmā me prajāḥ syur iti sa uttarāsu phalgunīṣv agnim ādadhītāryamṇo vā etad ahar yad uttarāḥ phalgunīr dānam aryamā dānakāmā asmai prajā bhavanti tāsu rājanyasyādadhyād dānaṃ hy eṣa prajānām upajīvati dānam aryamā dānakāmā asmai prajā bhavanti prajāpater vā etau stanau yat paurṇamāsī cāmāvāsyā ca yat paurṇamāsyāṃ vāmāvāsyāyāṃ vāgnim ādhatte prajāpatim eva prattaṃ duhe devānāṃ vā ete sadohavirdhāne yat paurṇamāsī cāmāvāsyā ca yat paurṇamāsyāṃ vāmāvāsyāyāṃ vāgnim ādhatta ubhe puṇyāhe ubhe yajñiye ||
children.translated_text: On the full moon of <s>Phalgunī</s> he should establish the fire for a Brahmin, for the full moon of <s>Phalgunī</s> is the face of the seasons; <s>Agni</s> is the face of the deities, and the Brahmin is the face of human beings. In summer he should establish it for a <s>rājanya</s>, for in summer <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>; and a <s>rājanya</s>, when he wishes to become pre-eminent, truly seeks to slay <s>Vṛtra</s>. In autumn he should establish it for a <s>vaiśya</s>; food is autumn, and by food the <s>vaiśya</s> becomes prosperous; he secures food to eat for him. If he were to establish it in another season, and if that one season were auspicious for him, then the others would be inauspicious and ill-wombed for him. Therefore, for one whose welfare he desires, he should establish it precisely on the full moon of <s>Phalgunī</s>; then all the seasons become auspicious for him, and all the seasons quicken him. This day of the full moon of <s>Phalgunī</s> is the mouth of the year. If he were to establish it on the day of the full moon of <s>Phalgunī</s>, he would set him in the very mouth of the year. The establishment should be two days before, or one day before; that takes hold of the second season and does not set him in the mouth of the year. And because it takes hold of the second season, he goes along stripping away the second power, the cattle, and the field of his rival, his kinsman-enemy. In the <s>Kṛttikās</s> he should establish it for a Brahmin. The <s>Kṛttikās</s> belong to <s>Agni</s>, and the Brahmin belongs to <s>Agni</s>; he establishes him in his own womb, on his own day. The <s>Kṛttikās</s> are the head of <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Agni</s> is the mouth, and food is eaten by means of the head and mouth. He secures food to eat for him. There are seven <s>Kṛttikās</s>; there are seven breaths in the head. He places the breaths in him. In <s>Rohiṇī</s> he should establish it for one who desires cattle. This is <s>Soma</s>'s nakṣatra, namely <s>Rohiṇī</s>; <s>Soma</s> is the seed-holder, and he places seed in him. This earth was indeed a star at first. On her, in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the gods made the plants grow. Therefore, just as these plants have grown upon her, so cattle grow in him who, knowing thus, establishes <s>Agni</s> in <s>Rohiṇī</s>. In <s>Rohiṇī</s> he should establish it for one who desires heaven; in <s>Rohiṇī</s> the gods went to the heavenly world, and he goes to the heavenly world itself. The <s>Kālakāñja</s> Asuras piled up bricks, thinking, 'We shall climb to heaven.' <s>Indra</s>, calling himself a Brahmin, approached them. He too set down this brick, as if they were first stepping up to heaven, and then he tore it away. Those Asuras, becoming worse off, fell down. The two who were highest became two dogs of <s>Yama</s>; those below became spiders. The brick that he tore away became <s>Citrā</s>. One who has a rival or a kinsman-enemy should establish <s>Agni</s> in <s>Citrā</s>. Just as, when that brick had been torn away, the Asuras became worse off and fell down, so his rival, his kinsman-enemy, becoming worse off, falls down, if he, knowing thus, establishes <s>Agni</s> in <s>Citrā</s>. One who should desire, 'May I be fortunate and an eater of food,' should establish <s>Agni</s> in the former <s>Phalgunīs</s>. This is <s>Bhaga</s>'s day, namely the former <s>Phalgunīs</s>; he becomes fortunate and an eater of food. But one who should desire, 'May my offspring be eager to give,' should establish <s>Agni</s> in the latter <s>Phalgunīs</s>. This is <s>Aryaman</s>'s day, namely the latter <s>Phalgunīs</s>; giving belongs to <s>Aryaman</s>, and his offspring become eager to give to him. In them he should establish it for a <s>rājanya</s>, for he lives upon the giving of the people. Giving belongs to <s>Aryaman</s>, and his people become eager to give to him. These two, the full moon and the new moon, are the two breasts of <s>Prajāpati</s>. When he establishes <s>Agni</s> on the full moon or on the new moon, he milks <s>Prajāpati</s> as one already given. These two, the full moon and the new moon, are the gods' two sitting-places and havirdhānas. When he establishes <s>Agni</s> on the full moon or on the new moon, both are meritorious days, both fit for sacrifice.

children.text: na purā sūryasyodetor manthitavā asuryo videvā ādhīyata udyatsu raśmiṣu mathyas tat sadevaḥ sendra ubhayor ahno rūpa ādhīyate caturviṃśatyāṃ prakrameṣv ādheyaś caturviṃśatyakṣarā vai gāyatrī gāyatram agneś chandaḥ sva evainaṃ yonau sve chandasy ādhatte tad yasyertsed aparimita eva tasyādadhyāt kṣeṣṇu vai parimitam aparimitam evāsmai jīvanam avarunddhe agnir vai sṛṣṭaḥ prajāpater adhy udakrāmat sa prajāpatir abibhed ada evāsā abhūd idam aham iti tasminn anuniṣkramyājuhod etarhi khalu vā eṣa sṛjyate yarhy ādhīyate tad āhur ramṇa evānudrutyāthāgnihotraṃ hotavyam iti tan naivaṃ kartavā ayataṃ tat kuṇḍyāgrīyaṃ tad yajñasya kriyate yad yoneḥ param avaraṃ kuryād aprajaniṣṇuḥ syāddhavīṃṣy eva pūrvāṇi nirupyātha sāyam agnihotraṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Not before sunrise should it be churned; if it were established when churned before sunrise, it would be asuric and without gods. It is churned while the rays are rising; then it is established with the gods, with <s>Indra</s>, in the form of both days. The establishment should be at twenty-four steps. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables, and the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter of <s>Agni</s>; he establishes him in his own womb, in his own meter. Therefore, for one whose welfare he desires, he should establish it at an unmeasured distance. What is measured is subject to decay; he secures unmeasured life for him. <s>Agni</s>, when created, went away from <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> was afraid, thinking, 'He has become that there, while I am this here.' Having gone out after him, he made an offering into him. Now, indeed, this fire is created when it is established. Therefore they say, 'After running after him from the pleasant place, the agnihotra is then to be offered.' That should not be done so. That is an unprepared, hearth-edge act done to the sacrifice. If one were to make what is lower than the womb earlier, he would be without procreation. Having first set out the oblations, he should then offer the evening agnihotra.
<s>Agni</s> is light; light is <s>Agni</s>. Svaha.

children.text: iti tat sāyaṃ jyotiṣā reto madhyato dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the evening he places seed in the middle by means of light.
The sun is light; light is the sun. Svaha.
Thus in the morning.

children.text: tat sāyaṃ jyotiṣā reto madhyato hitam ||
children.translated_text: That seed, placed in the middle by the evening light, he generated in the morning.

children.text: prātaḥ prajanayāmakar devāś ca vā asurāś ca saṃyattā āsann athendro 'gnim ādhatta te devā abibhayur ada evāsā agniṃ gopāyamāno 'gnihotraṃ gopāyamāno bhaviṣyati na nā upaiṣyaty abhi no jeṣyantīti te 'bruvan yad eva tvaṃ kiṃca karavo yaddhanā yaj jinā yad vindāsai tat te 'gnihotraṃ kurmo 'thehīti sa vā ait tasmād rājanyasyāgnihotram ahotavyaṃ yaddhyevaiṣa kiṃca karoti yaddhanti yaj jināti yad vindate yad enaṃ viśa upatiṣṭhante tad rājanyasyāgnihotraṃ hotavyaṃ rājanyasyāgnihotrā3n na hotavyā3m iti mīmāṃsante yaddhutvā na juhuyād vi yajñaṃ chindyāj jīyeta vā pra vā mīyeta paurṇamāsīm amāvāsyāṃ vā prati hotavyam atho agnyupasthānaṃ vācayitavyas tenāsya darśapūrṇamāsau saṃtatā avichinnau bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were contending. Then <s>Indra</s> established <s>Agni</s>. The gods became afraid, thinking, 'This one, guarding <s>Agni</s> and guarding the agnihotra, will be just like those others; he will not approach us, and they will defeat us.' They said, 'Whatever you do, whatever wealth you win, whatever you conquer, whatever you acquire, that we shall make your agnihotra; now go.' He went. Therefore a <s>rājanya</s>'s agnihotra should be offered: whatever he does, whatever he strikes down, whatever he conquers, whatever he acquires, whatever clans attend upon him, that is the <s>rājanya</s>'s agnihotra, and it should be offered. They deliberate, 'Should a <s>rājanya</s>'s agnihotra be offered, or should it not be offered?' If, after having offered it, he were not to continue offering, he would cut the sacrifice apart, or he would be defeated, or he would die. It should be offered at the full moon or at the new moon. And the fire-adoration formula should be recited; by that his darśa and pūrṇamāsa rites become continuous and unbroken.

children.translated_text: For the man of whom he wishes, 'May he possess cattle,' they should bring fire from the house of one who is richly nourished with many cattle. Just as cattle followed this one when he was being created, so cattle follow him when he is being brought; for <s>Agni</s> is <s>Rudra</s>. And for the man of whom he wishes, 'May he be an eater of food,' they should bring the southern fire from his roasting-pan; among fires this one is the eater of food, and the roasting-pan is the maker of food. He thereby secures food-eating for him. They say, 'As a low man, a native-born <s>puklaka</s>, might practise healing, so is this.' Therefore it is precisely one produced by friction; it becomes auspicious for the sacrificer and auspicious for the cattle. If one who is going to sacrifice with soma should establish the fire, he should not present oblations before a full year has passed, lest <s>Rudra</s> become one who threatens his cattle. These are cattle, namely rice and barley. Having cooked a four-dish mess of them, he should present it to the Brahmins as if it were living grain. If he did not offer to those deities for whom he establishes the fire, he would cut himself off from them and would become brooding and hungry. To them an offering of ghee should be made; by that he is not cut off from them, and he becomes free from brooding and free from hunger. After a year he presents the oblations. Then <s>Rudra</s>, being hidden within the year, does not injure his cattle. He offered the agnihotra for a year; he found that austerity, and together with all of it he mounted to the heavenly world. Three times, indeed, the <s>Virāj</s> strode here: the gārhapatya, the āhavanīya, and the sabhya fire. Thus he attained the <s>Virāj</s>. Food is the <s>Virāj</s>; he thereby attains food. For a <s>rājanya</s> he should offer in the middle of the gaming-ground with a verse to <s>Varuṇa</s>. <s>Varuṇa</s> is the king of the gods; he secures kingship for him. He offers after placing down gold; he offers where there is fire and where there is a proper place. The adhvaryu would be blind if he offered in a place that was no proper seat. He should give him a hundred dice, and he should sort them out. A man has a hundred years of life and a hundredfold vigor; he obtains life and vigor. On that day they should play in the assembly for his cow; they should not injure her limbs. He should present her to the members of the assembly. Whatever he wins with her should be given to the Brahmins. He thereby secures food belonging to the sabhya fire.
