children.translated_text: On the night after which, in the morning, he is to establish <s>Agni</s>, he should cook rice in four dishes during that night and offer it to Brahmins as if it were raw rice-grain. <s>Aditi</s>, desiring offspring, cooked rice; she ate what was left from it. From her <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Aryaman</s> were born. She cooked another; she ate what was left from it. From her <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> were born. She cooked another; she ate what was left from it. From her <s>Aṃśa</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> were born. She cooked another. She thought, 'When I eat what is left, two by two are born to me. Surely it would be better for me if I ate beforehand.' Having eaten beforehand, she offered it. While still within her as embryos they spoke: 'We two shall be this, namely <s>Ādityas</s>.' The <s>Ādityas</s> sought someone to strike them out; <s>Aṃśa</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> struck them out. Therefore these two are worshipped by sacrifice. The share-eating portion is the allotment of <s>Aṃśa</s>; <s>Bhaga</s> went among men. Therefore they say, 'One should go among men; there one meets with <s>Bhaga</s>.' He, indeed <s>Indra</s>, raised his breath upward; the other egg became dead. That, indeed, is <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>, whose offspring are these human beings. <s>Aditi</s> then ran to the <s>Ādityas</s>: 'Let this belong to me; let this not fall away from me in vain.' They said, 'Then let this one declare himself one of us; let him not slight us.' That, indeed, is <s>Vivasvān Āditya</s>, whose sons are <s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> and <s>Yama</s>. <s>Manu</s> is in this world, <s>Yama</s> in that one. These <s>Ādityas</s> guard the paths that lead to the gods. They thrust away the man who intends to sacrifice. Whoever establishes <s>Agni</s> without first announcing it to them, these thrust him away from the heavenly world. The <s>Ādityas</s> are sharers in what is left over. When, after turning the fuel-sticks about in what is left over, he lays them on, he thereby announces the agnyādheya (establishment of Agni) to the <s>Ādityas</s>; they do not thrust him away from the heavenly world. A man intending to establish <s>Agni</s> should let a year pass. They should not carry fire from his house, nor should they bring it from elsewhere. In a year embryos grow mature and are born; he establishes him as one born and mature. He should let twelve nights pass. The twelve nights are the counterpart of the year. In a year embryos grow mature and are born; he establishes him as one born and mature. He should let three nights pass. These worlds are three; he obtains these very worlds. He should let one night pass. <s>Prajāpati</s> is one; he obtains <s>Prajāpati</s> himself. <s>Purūravas Aiḍa</s> found the goddess <s>Urvaśī</s>; from her <s>Āyu</s> was born. He eagerly followed the gods to the heavenly world. They said, 'We are gods; where will this man go?' He said, 'I have many kinsmen; they will say of me, "What has this son of a goddess brought from the gods, his mother's brothers? Let there be something for me."' <s>Agni</s> gave him a sacrificial body. Placing it in his lap, he brought it away. He put it down in an ukhā (fire-pan). It became the shoot of the ashvattha tree; the ukhā became the shami tree. Therefore these two are fit for sacrificial use, for they are of auspicious birth. <s>Agni</s> came to <s>Varuṇa</s> for studentship while he was away; he lay with his wife. Watching for him as he came from the east, he ran away westward. <s>Varuṇa</s> knew, 'He is carrying off all virile power, strength, and seed, having stripped it away.' To undo that, he stripped it away. What was seed became the shoot of the ashvattha; what was the caul became the shami. Therefore these two are fit for sacrificial use, for they are of auspicious birth. <s>Prajāpati</s>, after creating creatures, thought himself emptied. Becoming a horse, he stood for a year with his head bent down toward the earth. From his head the ashvattha sprang up. That is why the ashvattha is called ashvattha. Therefore this tree is fit for sacrificial use, for it belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: manur vai prajākāmo 'gnim ādhāsyamāno devatāyai devatāyā ajuhot ||
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s>, desiring offspring and intending to establish <s>Agni</s>, made offerings to each deity in turn.
Then from the oblation to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Prapharvī</s> arose.
Ghee dripped from her feet.
She went to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tā abrūtām āhutyā vai tvam āvayor ajaniṣṭhā manos tvai tvam asi taṃ parehīti ||
children.translated_text: They said to her, 'You were born from our oblation; you belong to <s>Manu</s>. Go to him.'
She went to <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: so 'bravīd asurā vā ime puṇyamanyā agnim ādadhate tān parehīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'These <s>Asuras</s>, thinking themselves holy, are establishing <s>Agni</s>. Go to them.'
She went away.
They established that one first, then this one, then this one.
She came back.
He asked her, 'What did they come to?'

children.text: sābravīd amum evāgrā ādhiṣatāthemam athemam iti ||
children.translated_text: She said, 'They established that one first, then this one, then this one.'

children.text: so 'bravīt sakṛd vāvāsurāḥ śriyo 'ntam aguḥ parā tu bhaviṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'The <s>Asuras</s> have only once reached the limit of prosperity; but they will fall away.'

children.text: so 'bravīd devā vā ime puṇyamanyā agnim ādadhate tān parehīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'These gods, thinking themselves holy, are establishing <s>Agni</s>. Go to them.'
She went away.
They established this one first, then that one, then this one.
She came back.
He asked her, 'What did they come to?'

children.text: sābravīd imam evāgrā ādhiṣatāthāmum athemam iti ||
children.translated_text: She said, 'They established this one first, then that one, then this one.'

children.text: so 'bravīt sakṛd vāva devāḥ sarveṇa sākaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ samārukṣann itaḥpradānāt tu yajñam upajīviṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Surely once the gods ascended to the heavenly world together with everything; but from this time onward they will live by the sacrifice."

children.text: yaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dāsyant syāt sa imam agrā ādadhītāthāmum athemaṃ ||
children.translated_text: If there should be a man who is to give all his possessions, he should first establish this one, then that one, and then this one.

children.text: tad yathaiva devāḥ sarveṇa sākaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ samārohann evam eva yajamānaḥ sarveṇa sākaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ samārohati ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatte ||
children.translated_text: Just as the gods ascended to the heavenly world together with everything, so the sacrificer ascends to the heavenly world together with everything, when, knowing thus, he establishes <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: so 'bravīd ṛṣayo vā ime puṇyamanyā agnim ādadhate tān parehīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "These seers, thinking themselves meritorious, are establishing <s>Agni</s>; go to them."
She went away.
They first established this one, then this one, and then that one.
She came back again.
He asked her, "What did they do?"

children.text: sābravīd imam evāgrā ādhiṣatāthemam athāmum iti ||
children.translated_text: She said, "They first established this one, then this one, and then that one."

children.text: so 'bravīd ahaṃ vāvāgnyādheyaṃ vidāṃcakāra sarveṣu vā eṣu lokeṣv ṛṣayaḥ pratyaṣṭhur iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "I indeed have understood the agnyādheya; the seers have taken their stand in all these worlds."

children.text: prati prajayā ca paśubhiś ca tiṣṭhati ya evaṃ vidvān agnim ādhatte ||
children.translated_text: He takes his stand with offspring and with cattle, when, knowing thus, he establishes <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yad amum ādhāyemam ādadhyād apa tad ādadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: If, after establishing that one, he were to establish this one, he would establish it wrongly.

children.text: yad vāvemam ādhāyāmum ādadhyād apa tad ādadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or if, after establishing this one, he were to establish that one, he would establish it wrongly.
Therefore he should establish this one first, then this one, and then that one.
In that way the rite is performed in prosperity.
The establishment should be on ground sloping eastward.
In that way the rite is performed in prosperity.
It should be established east of the middle bamboo pole.
In that way the rite is performed in prosperity.

children.text: yā vai sā prapharvy āsīt sā gaur abhavat ||
children.translated_text: She who was that prapharvī became a cow.
She is <s>Iḍā</s>, the human one, ghee-footed, belonging to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: yat tvā kruddhaḥ parovapa manyunā sumanastara
children.translated_text: When, being angry, you cast away, through wrath, O more kindly one,

children.text: sukalpam agne tat tava punas tvoddīpayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: that auspicious form of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, we kindle you again.
When you, cast away by wrath, ran after the earth,

children.text: ādityā viśve tad devā vasavaḥ punar ābharan ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s> brought that back again.

children.text: yat te bhāmena vicakarānīśāno hṛdas pari
children.translated_text: What, through your fury, you tore apart from around the heart, as lord,

children.text: punas tad indraś cāgniś ca vasavaḥ samacīkﾱpan ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s>, restored again.

children.text: punas tvādityā rudrā vasavaḥ samindhatāṃ punar brahmāṇo vasudhīte agne
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and <s>Vasus</s> kindle you again; again let the brahmans kindle you, O wealth-bearing <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: ghṛtena tvaṃ tanvaṃ vardhayasva rāyaspoṣā yajamānaṃ sacantām ||
children.translated_text: With ghee strengthen your body; let wealth and nourishment accompany the sacrificer.

children.text: trayastriṃśat tantavo yaṃ vitanvata imaṃ ca yajñaṃ sudhayā dadante
children.translated_text: The thirty-three strands which they stretch out, and this sacrifice which they place with good ordering,

children.text: tebhiś chidram apidadhmo yad atra svāhā yajño apyetu devān ||
children.translated_text: with them we cover the breach here. Svāhā; let the sacrifice go to the gods.

children.text: mano jyotir juṣatām ājyasya vicchinnaṃ yajñaṃ sam imaṃ dadhātu
children.translated_text: Let mind, the light, enjoy the ghee; let it put together this interrupted sacrifice.

children.text: imaṃ yajñaṃ saptatantuṃ tataṃ nā ā devā yantu sumanasyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the gods, becoming well-disposed, come to this sacrifice of ours, stretched out with seven strands.

children.text: bṛhaspatir no haviṣā ghṛtena vicchinnaṃ yajñaṃ sam imaṃ dadhātu
children.translated_text: May <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, with our oblation and with ghee, put together this interrupted sacrifice.

children.text: yā iṣṭā uṣaso yāś ca yājyās tāḥ saṃdadhāmi manasā ghṛtena ||
children.translated_text: The offerings that have been made, and those that are morning offerings, and those that are to be sacrificed: these I join together with mind and with ghee.

children.text: agne 'bhyāvartinn abhi māvartasvāyuṣā varcasā prajayā dhanena sanyā medhayā rayyā poṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, turn back toward me, turn back to me with life, with radiance, with offspring, with wealth, together with insight, riches, and nourishment.

children.text: agne aṅgiraḥ śataṃ te santv āvṛtaḥ sahasraṃ ta upāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni Aṅgiras</s>, let there be a hundred turnings for you, a thousand returnings for you.

children.text: athā poṣasya poṣeṇa punar no naṣṭam ākṛdhi punar no rayim ākṛdhi ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the nourishment of nourishment, make again for us what was lost; make wealth for us again.

children.text: punar ūrjā nivartasva punar agna iṣāyuṣā
children.translated_text: Turn back again with vigor; turn back again, O <s>Agni</s>, with refreshment and life.
Protect us again from distress.
Turn back together with wealth, O <s>Agni</s>; swell with a stream,
all-nourishing, from every side.

children.text: salilaḥ saligaḥ sagaras te na ādityā haviṣo juṣāṇā vyantu svāhā ketaḥ suketaḥ saketas te na ādityā haviṣo juṣāṇā vyantu svāhā devajūte vivasvann āditya te no devāḥ satyāṃ devahūtiṃ deveṣv āsuvadhvam ādityebhyaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Salila</s>, <s>Saliga</s>, and <s>Sagara</s>: through them may the <s>Ādityas</s>, enjoying the oblation, come here. Svāhā. <s>Keta</s>, <s>Suketa</s>, and <s>Saketa</s>: through them may the <s>Ādityas</s>, enjoying the oblation, come here. Svāhā. O god-impelled <s>Vivasvant Āditya</s>, may the gods set our true invocation of the gods among the gods. Svāhā to the <s>Ādityas</s>.
The punarādheya is indeed the portion of <s>Agni</s>.
Seeking to obtain this portion, one causes failure.

children.text: yady ādadhāno manyeta vi syā ṛdhyatā ity utsādya punar ādadhīta ||
children.translated_text: If, while establishing the fire, he should think, "May it be disjoined; may it prosper," then, after causing it to go out, he should establish it again.

children.text: yam eva bhāgaṃ prepsan vyardhayati taṃ prāpyārdhayaty eva ||
children.translated_text: The very portion which, seeking to obtain, he causes to fail, having obtained that, he makes it prosper.
Everything is made to belong to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yat kiṃca sarvam evāgnaye bhāgaṃ pradāya sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever there is, after giving all of it as a portion to <s>Agni</s>, he obtains every prosperity.

children.text: na saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhṛtyā na yajuḥ kartavā ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The materials should not be gathered, nor should a yajus be performed."
For this one has his materials already gathered and his yajus already performed.

children.text: tad āhuḥ saṃbhṛtyā eva saṃbhārāḥ kāryaṃ yajur iti ||
children.translated_text: They say this instead: "The materials should indeed be gathered, and a yajus should be performed."

children.text: punarutsyūtaṃ vāso deyaṃ punarṇavo rathaḥ punarutsṛṣṭo 'naḍvān ||
children.translated_text: A garment sewn up again should be given, a chariot made new again, and a draught ox released again.
These are indeed the forms of the punarādheya.
Having obtained its forms, he secures it for himself.

children.text: agnir vā utsīdann apa oṣadhīr abhyutsīdati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, when going out, goes out toward the waters and plants.
Darbha grasses are waters and plants.

children.text: yad darbhā upolapā bhavanty adbhya evainam oṣadhībhyo 'dhy āptvāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: When the darbha grasses are strewn near, having obtained him from the waters and plants, he secures him for himself.

children.text: devā asurair vijayam upayanto 'gnau priyās tanvaḥ saṃnyadadhata ||
children.translated_text: The gods, going forth to victory against the asuras, deposited their dear bodies in <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yan no jayeyur imā abhyupadhāvema yady u jayememā abhyupāvartemahīti ||
children.translated_text: They thought, "If they should conquer us, we will run back to these; but if we should conquer, we will turn back to these."
Having conquered, the gods sought them out.
They said, "They belong to all of us together."

children.text: so 'gnir abravīd ya eva māṃ maddevatya ādadhātai sa etābhis tanūbhiḥ saṃbhavād iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Agni</s> said, "Whoever establishes me as belonging to my deity will come together with these bodies."
The gods established him.
They came together with these bodies.
Cattle are indeed the dear bodies of the gods.
With cattle, then, they came together.

children.text: tad ya evaṃ vidvān punarādheyam ādhatta etābhir evāgnes tanūbhiḥ saṃbhavati ||
children.translated_text: The man who, knowing thus, establishes the renewed fire becomes united with these very bodies of <s>Agni</s>.
Cattle are indeed the dear bodies of the gods.
He thereby becomes united with cattle.
<s>Manu</s>, desiring prosperity, established the fire.
He nourished these forms of nourishment.
Through that he prospered.
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, desiring cattle, established the fire.
Then these cattle belonging to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> were born.
Through that he prospered.
<s>Prajāpati</s>, desiring offspring, established the fire.
Then these creatures belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s> were born.
Through that he prospered.

children.text: yo vai tam agrā ādhatta sa tena vasunā samabhavat ||
children.translated_text: Whoever established it first became possessed of that wealth.
That is why <s>Punarvasu</s> has the nature of renewed wealth.
Therefore the establishment should be performed under <s>Punarvasu</s>.

children.text: punar hi sa tena vasunā samabhavat ||
children.translated_text: For through that wealth he again became possessed of wealth.
Whoever established it prospered through it.
Therefore the establishment should be performed under the <s>Anurādhās</s>, for prosperity.
He surely prospers, and also for pairing.
<s>Svarbhānu</s> the Asura struck the sun with darkness.
The gods struck away that darkness from it.
When they struck away the first darkness, it became a black ewe.
When they struck away the second, it became red.
When the third, it became white.
What they cut away from above became a barren ewe.
The gods said, 'Let us take this divine animal for our desire.'

children.text: atha vā iyaṃ tarhy ṛkṣāsīd alomikā ||
children.translated_text: Now this earth at that time was a star, without hair.

children.text: te 'bruvaṃs tasmai kāmāyālabhāmahai yathāsyām oṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca jāyantā iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'Let us take it for that desire, so that plants and forest trees may be born upon it.'
They did indeed take it for that desire.
Thereafter plants and forest trees were born upon it.

children.text: yaḥ prajākāmo vā paśukāmo vā syāt sa etām aviṃ vaśām ālabheta ||
children.translated_text: If a man desires offspring or desires cattle, he should take this barren ewe.

children.text: pra prajayā ca paśubhiś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: He is born forth with offspring and with cattle.

children.text: atho āhur yaḥ prathamas tamasy apahate sūryasya raśmir yūpasya caṣāle 'vātanot sāvir vaśābhavad iti ||
children.translated_text: They also say, 'The first ray of the sun, when the darkness was struck away, stretched down upon the cup of the sacrificial post; that became the barren ewe.'
Thus in both ways the divine animal is taken.

children.text: yady asyās taj janma yadi vetaraṃ tat kāmāya kāmāyaivāvir vaśālabhyate ||
children.translated_text: Whether that is its birth or whether the other is, the barren ewe is taken for each and every desire.
He should take a goat for <s>Agni</s> and a ram for <s>Varuṇa</s>.
He should sacrifice for one who desires prosperity.
The bones of a man are indeed connected with <s>Agni</s>.
The flesh is connected with <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: āgneyenaivāsyāgneyaṃ niṣkrīṇāti vāruṇena vāruṇaṃ bhavaty eva ||
children.translated_text: With what belongs to <s>Agni</s> he thereby buys off what in him belongs to <s>Agni</s>; with what belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>, what belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>. He indeed becomes prosperous.

children.text: sārasvatīṃ meṣīm ālabheta yo vāco gṛhīta ||
children.translated_text: He should take a ewe for <s>Sarasvatī</s> for a man whose speech has been seized.
Speech is indeed <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
With speech itself he heals his speech.
It is one with no teeth fallen out, for completeness.
It is one not mounted, for full prosperity.

children.text: śvetā malhā ālabheta brahmavarcasakāma āgneyīṃ bārhaspatyāṃ saurīṃ vasantāgneyīṃ prāvṛṣi bārhaspatyāṃ śiśire saurīm ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brahmanic splendor should take white barren cows: one for <s>Agni</s>, one for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and one for <s>Sūrya</s>; in spring the one for <s>Agni</s>, in the rainy season the one for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, in winter the one for <s>Sūrya</s>.
In that it is for <s>Agni</s>, he secures brilliance by it.
In that it is for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, brahmanic splendor by it.
In that it is for <s>Sūrya</s>, radiance by it.

children.text: trivṛd vāvāsmā etat samṛddhaṃ brahmavarcasaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: In this way he places in him brahmanic splendor, prosperously made threefold.
They are taken around the year.
For by the year what has not been obtained is obtained.
Having obtained it for him through the year, he places brilliance and brahmanic splendor in him.
It is white; whiteness is the form of brahman, for prosperity.

children.text: vāyavyām ajām ālabheta sārasvatīṃ meṣīm adityā ajām abhiśasyamānaṃ yājayet ||
children.translated_text: He should take a goat for <s>Vāyu</s>, a ewe for <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and a goat for <s>Aditi</s>; he should sacrifice for a man who is being accused.

children.text: vāyur vā etasyāślīlaṃ gandhaṃ janatā anuviharati yam abhiśaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> indeed carries around among the people the foul smell of the man whom they accuse.
For he reaches all this.

children.text: yad vāyave vāyur evāsya taṃ gandhaṃ surabhim akaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that the offering is for <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Vāyu</s> himself makes that smell of his fragrant.
That fragrant smell of his spreads among the people.

children.text: vācā vā etam abhiśaṃsanti yam abhiśaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: With speech they accuse the man whom they accuse.
Speech is <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
In that it is for <s>Sarasvatī</s>, with speech itself she quiets their speech.
The man whom they accuse is indeed without foundation.
This earth is <s>Aditi</s>.
This earth is foundation.
In that it is for <s>Aditi</s>, he stands firm upon this very earth.

children.text: indriyeṇa vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yam abhiśaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: The man whom they accuse is deprived of faculty and virile power.
The embryo is faculty and virile power.
In that they are pregnant, with faculty and virile power they make him prosper.
You are earth by birth, a barren cow.
You have held <s>Agni</s> as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are atmosphere by birth, a barren cow.
You have held <s>Vāyu</s> as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are heaven by birth, a barren cow.
You have held <s>Āditya</s> as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are the stars by birth, a barren cow.
You have held the moon as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are the <s>Ṛg</s> by birth, a barren cow.
You have held the <s>Sāman</s> as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are the clan by birth, a barren cow.
You have held the king as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are speech by birth, a barren cow.
You have held breath as an embryo.
Become united with me.
You are the waters by birth, a barren cow.
You have held the sacrifice as an embryo.
Become united with me.
He sets down the one containing the threefold formula in front.
The threefold is indeed the mouth of the sacrifice.
Thus he places the mouth of the sacrifice at the front, from the mouth.
He sets down the one containing the seventeenfold formula on the south side.
Food indeed is the seventeenfold one.
Indeed, he places this food on the southern side.
Therefore food is eaten with the right hand.
Therefore the right half of the self is more vigorous.
Therefore birds turn around toward the right half.
One provided with the fifteenfold one is placed to the north.
Vital power indeed is the fifteenfold one.
Indeed, he places this vital power on the northern side.
One provided with the twenty-onefold one is placed behind, for firm standing.
He sets down one provided with the threefold one in front.
The threefold one is indeed the mouth of the sacrifice.
Indeed, he places the mouth of the sacrifice at its mouth.
He sets down one provided with the fifteenfold one on the southern side.
One provided with the seventeenfold one is placed on the northern side.
This is so that the two wings may possess vigor.
And also so that they may have their proper seat.
Therefore food is eaten with both hands.
And moreover the fifteenfold one is indeed a thunderbolt.

children.text: vajreṇa vā etad yajamāno bhrātṛvyam ubhayato nirbhajati ||
children.translated_text: With the thunderbolt the sacrificer thereby drives away his rival, his kinsman-enemy, on both sides.
One provided with the twenty-onefold one is placed behind, for firm standing.
For the twenty-onefold one is firm standing.
This is arranged according to the ordering of the <s>Arka</s>.
The <s>Arka</s> is food.
He for whom these are laid down becomes an eater of food.

children.text: agner bhāgo 'si dīkṣāyā ādhipatyaṃ brahma spṛtaṃ trivṛt stomā iti ||
children.translated_text: You are the share of <s>Agni</s>, the sovereignty of consecration, brahman touched, with the threefold stomas: thus he says.
These bricks indeed are named 'touched.'

children.text: etābhir vai prajāpatir yadyad akāmayata tattad aspṛṇot ||
children.translated_text: With these <s>Prajāpati</s> obtained whatever he desired.

children.text: yadyad evaitābhir yajamānaḥ kāmayate tattat spṛṇoty ekayāstuvata ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the sacrificer desires with these, that he obtains, by one who praises.
Creatures were set in place: thus he says.
These bricks indeed are named 'creations.'

children.text: etābhir vai prajāpatir yadyad akāmayata tattad asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: With these <s>Prajāpati</s> created whatever he desired.

children.text: yadyad evaitābhir yajamānaḥ kāmayate tattat sṛjate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the sacrificer desires with these, that he creates.

children.text: agne jātān praṇudā naḥ sapatnān iti ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, drive away from us the born rivals: thus he says.
He sets it down in front.

children.text: ya eva jātāḥ sapatnās tān etayā praṇudate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever rivals have already been born, with this he drives them away.
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, drive back the unborn: thus he says behind.

children.text: ya eva jātāḥ sapatnās tān etayā pratinudate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever rivals have already been born, with this he drives them back.
That indeed is the driving away of the rival, the kinsman-enemy.
The stoma is forty-fourfold.
Splendor and wealth: thus he says and sets it down on the southern side.
The stoma is sixteenfold.
Vital power and wealth: thus he says on the northern side.
The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> indeed has forty-four syllables.
The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is a thunderbolt.
The sixteenfold one is a thunderbolt.
The thunderbolt is grasped with the left and hurled with the right.

children.text: savyāpagrahaṇaṃ vā etad vajraṃ dakṣiṇāpraharaṇaṃ yajamāno bhrātṛvyāya praharati ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificer thereby hurls this thunderbolt, grasped with the left and hurled with the right, against his rival, his kinsman-enemy.
He sets down the one containing purīṣa in the middle.
For this is like purīṣa in the middle of the animal.
Purīṣa is the middle of the self.
He thus builds up <s>Agni</s> together with a self.
Now these are virāj-verses.
Speech indeed is <s>Virāj</s>.
These bricks indeed are cattle.

children.text: paśuṣu vā etad uttamāṃ vācaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He thereby places the highest speech among the cattle.
Therefore a man who has cattle speaks the highest speech.
This man, so-and-so, descendant of so-and-so, has been consecrated: thus he says.
He utters it aloud, as it were.
The consecrated man is dear to the gods.
He thereby announces him to the gods.
He says it three times.
For the gods belong to the threefold truth.
And moreover these worlds are three.
He thereby announces him to these worlds.
Therefore people hear a consecrated man from afar.
For he announces him to these worlds.
Having seen a nakṣatra, he releases his speech.

children.text: dvau vā ṛtū ahaś ca rātriś ca ||
children.translated_text: There are two seasons: day and night.

children.text: anyam eva ṛtuṃ samprāpya vācaṃ visṛjate ||
children.translated_text: Having reached another season, he releases his speech.
Undertake the vow: thus he releases his speech.
For this is his vow.
The sacrifice is held together by the vow.
By the vow he holds the sacrifice together.

children.text: daivīṃ dhiyaṃ manāmahā iti yajuṣā hastā avanenikte yajuṣā hi manuṣyā avanenijate vyāvṛttyai brahmaṇaḥ sadevatvāya ||
children.translated_text: With the yajus 'Let us think the divine thought' he washes his hands; for with a yajus human beings wash themselves, for distinction and so that the brahman may be accompanied by the gods.

children.text: atho āpo me dīkṣāṃ net pramuṣṇān iti ||
children.translated_text: And moreover he says, 'May the waters not rob me of my consecration.'
Food once withdrew in disgust from human beings.
The gods wished to place it among human beings.

children.text: tad āpo 'bruvan vayaṃ va etāṃ śundhāmāthopāvartasveti ||
children.translated_text: The waters said, 'We shall purify this for you; then let it turn back.'
Then food turned back to human beings.
So this food is held among human beings.
Therefore a Brahmin is to be fed.
When it has been brought, he should wash his hands.
This is for securing the eating of food.

children.text: atho annāya vā etad ātmānaṃ pāvayate ||
children.translated_text: And moreover he thereby purifies himself for food.

children.text: ye devā manujātā manoyujā iti vrataṃ vratayaty ete vai devā manujātā manoyujo yad ime prāṇā eṣā vā asminn etarhi devatā ||
children.translated_text: With 'The gods born of Manu, yoked by mind,' he consecrates the vow; for these gods born of Manu and yoked by mind are these breaths, and this is the deity in him at this time.
He satisfies it.
In that deity he consecrates what has been offered.
If he were to consecrate the vow otherwise than from here, he would deprive him of the breaths.
He would be one whose life is cut short.

children.text: tvam agne vratapā asīti vadet svapsyant suptvā vā prabudhya yadi vā dīkṣitavādaṃ vadet ||
children.translated_text: He should say, 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the guardian of the vow,' when he is about to sleep, or after sleeping, when he wakes, or if he should speak consecrated speech.
<s>Agni</s> indeed is the guardian of the vow among the gods.
From him therefore he takes hold of the vow.
He should not lie on his back.
If he were to lie on his back, these worlds would go away.
He should not turn away from <s>Agni</s> with his back toward him.
If he were to turn away, he would turn away from the sacrifice.
The sun should neither set upon nor rise upon one who is elsewhere than the consecrated enclosure, one who has measured out the consecrated place.
That indeed is the vow of the consecrated man.
The sacrifice, indeed, did not come into being for the gods.
Servants brought it into being for them.
When he chooses the bhṛti (hire, service-payment), it is for the coming-into-being of the sacrifice.

children.text: rāsveyat someti yad brūyād etāvad asya syān na bhūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he were to say, 'Bring just this, O <s>Soma</s>,' only so much would be his, and no more.
When he says, 'Bring more,' it is for securing what is unlimited.

children.text: devaḥ savitā vasor vasudāveti savitṛprasūta evaitābhir devatābhir upa pratigṛhṇāty ātmano 'hiṃsāyai ||
children.translated_text: 'The god <s>Savitṛ</s>, giver of wealth, bestower of goods': impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, through these deities he receives it close at hand, for the non-injury of himself.
<s>Vāyu</s> is the protector; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the overlord.
<s>Pūṣan</s> is the receiver.

children.text: vāyum evāsāṃ goptāram akas tvaṣṭāram adhipatiṃ pūṣaṇaṃ pratigrahītāram ||
children.translated_text: He thereby makes <s>Vāyu</s> their protector, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> their overlord, and <s>Pūṣan</s> their receiver.
The waters, indeed, are the sacrifice.
If the consecrated man were to enter the waters, he would tear away the sacrifice.

children.text: yad āha devīr āpo apāṃ napād iti ||
children.translated_text: When he says, 'Divine waters, offspring of the waters,'

children.text: yad evāsāṃ yajñiyaṃ medhyaṃ tan nākrāmati ||
children.translated_text: he does not step upon whatever in them is sacrificial and ritually pure.
If the consecrated man were to enter the waters, they would become eddying and unsettled.
Therefore he should not enter them.
If he should enter them, he should cross while rubbing a clod of earth.
He crosses along that very bridge.

children.text: na vai dīkṣitaṃ tarantaṃ devatā anutaranti ||
children.translated_text: The deities do not cross after a consecrated man who is crossing.
He crosses together with the two fire-drills.
Thus he crosses together with the deities themselves.
The sacrifice does not cross after a consecrated man who is crossing.
He crosses together with a chariot-wheel.
Thus he crosses together with the sacrifice itself.

children.text: śādaṃ dadbhir avakān dantamūlair mṛdaṃ barsvai stegān daṃṣṭrābhyām avakrandena tālu vājaṃ hanubhyāṃ sarasvatyā agrajihvaṃ jihvāyā utsādam apa āsyena vṛṣaṇā āṇḍābhyām ādityāñ śmaśrubhiḥ panthāṃ bhrūbhyāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī vartobhyāṃ vidyutaṃ kanīnikābhyāṃ karṇābhyāṃ śrotre śrotrābhyāṃ karṇā avāryāṇi pakṣmāṇi pāryā ikṣavaḥ pāryāṇi pakṣmāṇy avāryā ikṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He assigns marsh-grass to the teeth, avakā grass to the roots of the teeth, clay to the barsu hairs, stegā plants to the tusks, the palate to the cry, strength to the jaws, <s>Sarasvatī</s> to the forepart of the tongue, the uplift to the tongue, waters to the mouth, the <s>Vṛṣaṇas</s> to the testicles, the <s>Ādityas</s> to the beard-hairs, the path to the eyebrows, heaven and earth to the eyelids, lightning to the pupils, the powers of hearing to the ears, the ears to the organs of hearing, the lower eyelashes as avārya reeds, the upper reeds as pārya reeds, the upper eyelashes as pārya reeds, and the lower reeds as avārya reeds.

children.text: indrasya kroḍo 'dityāḥ pājasyaṃ diśāṃ jatravo 'dityā bhasad jīmūtān hṛdayaupaśābhyām antarikṣaṃ pulītatā nabha udaryeṇa valmīkān klomnā glaubhir gulmāṃś cakravākau matasnābhyāṃ divaṃ vṛkkābhyāṃ hirābhiḥ sravantīr girīn plāśibhyām upalān plīhnā hradān kukṣibhyāṃ samudram udareṇa vaiśvānaraṃ bhasmanā ||
children.translated_text: The hollow is <s>Indra</s>'s; the rib-region belongs to <s>Aditi</s>; the collarbones belong to the quarters; the buttock belongs to <s>Aditi</s>; the rain-clouds are assigned to the two heart-supports, the atmosphere to the pulītatā, the sky to the belly, anthills to the lungs, thickets to the spleen-like parts, the two cakravāka birds to the kidneys, heaven to the two kidneys, the flowing rivers to the veins, mountains to the plāśi organs, stones to the spleen, pools to the flanks, the ocean to the belly, and <s>Vaiśvānara</s> to the ash.
